title: changedetection.io alternatives in 2026: move to Firecrawl
summary: Compare changedetection.io alternatives, from Firecrawl /monitor to Visualping, Distill.io, urlwatch and Huginn, and move your watches in minutes.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR**


- **Firecrawl /monitor is the changedetection.io alternative that needs no server and no model key.** It checks pages, whole sites or web searches on your schedule, judges each change against a goal you write in plain English, and alerts by email, Slack or webhook. You can set it up in the dashboard, through the API, or in ChatGPT, Claude and Grok Bot, and the[free plan](https://www.firecrawl.dev/pricing) includes 1,000 Firecrawl credits a month.
- **changedetection.io is an open-source change monitor you run with Docker, plus an $8.99 a month hosted plan.** It watches pages or page elements with CSS, XPath and text filters, and sends alerts through a long list of notification services.
- **People switch when the setup grows.** JavaScript pages and Browser Steps need a separate Chrome or Playwright browser, AI summaries need your own model provider key, and self-hosting leaves updates and uptime with you.


---


If you're moving off changedetection.io, Firecrawl /monitor is where I'd start. You keep the schedule, the diffs and the alerts, and you drop the server, the browser container and the model key. Below is what changedetection.io does well, why people switch, and five more alternatives, from hosted apps to open-source tools you run yourself. For the wider category, see our roundup of the[best website change detection tools](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/best-website-change-detection-tools) .


## What is changedetection.io?


changedetection.io is an open-source website change monitor that you run on your own server with Docker or Python, or use through a hosted plan from its developers. It checks each page on a schedule, compares it with the previous version, and alerts you when the part of the page you selected changes.


- CSS and XPath selectors, plus trigger text and ignore text filters
- Restock and price alerts for product pages
- Browser Steps that click, fill in fields and run searches before a check
- Alerts through Discord, Slack, Telegram, email, webhooks and many other services
- AI summaries and notification rules when you add your own model provider key


Self-hosting is free under the Apache-2.0 license. The hosted plan costs $8.99 a month for up to 5,000 URLs, with re-checks from about every 5 minutes and one Chrome browser for JavaScript pages.


## Why do people look for changedetection.io alternatives?


People look for changedetection.io alternatives when running it takes more effort than the alerts are worth. The usual triggers are server upkeep, the extra browser service that JavaScript pages need, and AI features that depend on a separate model account and key.


**You own the server.** A self-hosted install is yours to update, back up and restart. When a release changes something, you find out on your own hardware.


**JavaScript pages need a second service.** The built-in fetcher reads plain HTML. Pages that load content with JavaScript, the Visual Selector and Browser Steps all need a Playwright or WebDriver browser, which the project's[Playwright content fetcher guide](https://github.com/dgtlmoon/changedetection.io/wiki/Playwright-content-fetcher) runs as its own Chrome service next to changedetection.io. The same guide notes that the Playwright browser can grow from 200 MB to several gigabytes of memory, and suggests restarting the service on a schedule. The hosted plan includes one Chrome browser, and you add more as you need them.


**AI needs your own model.** AI summaries and notification rules run on a key from a hosted provider such as OpenAI, Anthropic or Google Gemini, or on a local Ollama model you run yourself. A hosted key means one more account and bill, and a local model means one more service to keep running.

## What are the best changedetection.io alternatives in 2026?


The best changedetection.io alternatives in 2026 are Firecrawl /monitor for AI-judged alerts with no server, Visualping and PageCrawl.io for hosted monitoring, Distill.io for checks from your own browser, and urlwatch and Huginn for open-source setups you run yourself.


### 1. Firecrawl /monitor


[Firecrawl /monitor](https://www.firecrawl.dev/monitor) runs scheduled checks on pages, whole sites or web searches and sends only what changed to you, your inbox or your agent. It runs on the same engine as[Firecrawl /scrape](https://www.firecrawl.dev/scrape) , so JavaScript pages are rendered on every check with no browser container to manage.


changedetection.io Firecrawl /monitor


**Wins on** Free self-hosting and a long list of notification services AI judging included, whole-site and web search monitors, setup from AI assistants


**Where it runs** Your server with Docker, or the $8.99 a month hosted plan Firecrawl Cloud, with the open-source engine also available for your own server


**JavaScript pages** A Playwright or Chrome browser service Rendered on every check


**What it watches** Pages and page elements Pages, whole sites and new results across the web


**Noise filtering** CSS, XPath, trigger text and ignore text A plain-English goal with an AI verdict, plus field-level JSON tracking


**AI** Your own model provider key Included, 1 Firecrawl credit per changed page judged


**Alerts** Discord, Slack, Telegram, email, webhooks and more Email summaries, Slack and webhooks


**Setup** Web UI and API Dashboard, REST API, Python and Node SDKs, CLI, MCP server, ChatGPT, Claude and Grok Bot


Each check labels every page as same, new, changed, removed or error. When you add a goal, an AI judge reads each changed page and returns whether the change matters, a confidence level and a reason, so a rotating banner or a timestamp stays quiet. For prices and stock levels, JSON mode tracks the fields you define and reports each one as a previous and current value, which covers the restock and price alerts changedetection.io users rely on.


- **Three scopes:** page monitors for known URLs, website monitors that crawl a site for added, changed and removed pages, and web-scale monitors that run recurring searches. The[web-scale monitoring launch post](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/web-monitoring-launch) covers the third.
- **Schedules in plain text:**` every 30 minutes` ,` daily at 9am` or cron, from every 5 minutes up, with up to 50 targets per monitor.
- **Alerts where you work:** email summaries that skip checks with no meaningful change, Slack from the dashboard, and webhooks that arrive as each page finishes.

### 2. Visualping


Visualping is a hosted monitoring app that compares pages visually and as text, with nothing to install. Its free plan covers 5 pages and 150 checks a month at most once an hour, and Personal plans start at $14 a month for 10 pages.


- AI change summaries on every plan
- A Chrome extension that records steps such as clicks, then replays them before each check
- REST API and MCP server access on every plan, including the free one


**Best for:** people who want visual alerts on a handful of pages without running anything.


### 3. Distill.io


Distill.io watches whole pages or selected elements from a browser extension, a desktop app or its cloud. Local monitors run in your own browser, with intervals from 5 seconds. Its free plan includes 25 monitors, 5 of them in the cloud with checks every 6 hours.


- Actions that run on a page before a check
- Email, push, SMS and webhook alerts
- Unlimited checks from the browser extension


**Best for:** individuals who track a few pages from the browser they already use.


### 4. PageCrawl.io


PageCrawl.io is a hosted monitoring service built for teams that watch hundreds or thousands of pages. Its free plan tracks 6 pages with 220 checks a month, and paid plans are billed yearly, starting at $160 a year.


- AI summaries and filtering, with a monthly allowance per plan
- Actions such as clicks and typing before a check
- Roles, SSO and review boards for teams


**Best for:** teams that want a fixed yearly price for a large page count.


### 5. urlwatch


urlwatch is an open-source command-line tool, written in Python, that watches pages or parts of pages and reports what changed. You list jobs in a config file and run them from cron or another scheduler, and browser jobs load a page in a real browser before comparing it.


**Best for:** developers who want every watch in a config file under version control.


### 6. Huginn


Huginn is an open-source automation system, released under the MIT license, where you build agents that read the web, watch for events and take actions. One agent can scrape a site and email you when it changes, and others can pass that event on to a webhook or a chat message. The quickest start is its official Docker image.


**Best for:** people who want change alerts to trigger further steps, on their own server.


## How do you move from changedetection.io to Firecrawl /monitor?


Moving from changedetection.io to Firecrawl /monitor takes a list of your watch URLs and one monitor. You can create it in the Firecrawl dashboard, ask ChatGPT, Claude or Grok Bot to create it, or run a short script that reads your watches from the changedetection.io API and sends them to the Firecrawl SDK.


### How do you set up Firecrawl /monitor in the dashboard?


The dashboard needs no code:


- Open the[monitoring dashboard](https://www.firecrawl.dev/app/monitoring) and create a monitor.
- Paste the URLs from your changedetection.io watch list, or pick a site or a search to watch.
- Set a schedule and write your goal in plain English.
- Choose where alerts go: email, Slack or a webhook.


### How do you set up Firecrawl /monitor in ChatGPT, Claude or Grok Bot?


Add Firecrawl to the AI assistant you already use, then describe the monitor in plain English:


- **ChatGPT and Grok Bot:** install the Firecrawl plugin for[ChatGPT](https://www.firecrawl.dev/integrations/chatgpt) or[Grok Bot](https://www.firecrawl.dev/integrations/grok-bot) .
- **Claude:** add` https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth` as a custom connector and sign in with your Firecrawl account. Use the custom connector, since it includes the monitor tools.
- **Claude Code:** run` claude mcp add --transport http firecrawl https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth` , then sign in from` /mcp` .
- **Codex CLI:** run` codex mcp add firecrawl --url https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth` , then` codex mcp login firecrawl` .
- **Cursor and other MCP clients:** add the same server URL to your MCP settings.


Then paste your watch list into a brief like this one:


```text
Use Firecrawl to monitor these pages every 6 hours and email me at
me@example.com when a price, plan or new entry changes. Ignore dates,
banners and layout edits. Show me the monitor's monthly credit estimate.
https://example.com/pricing
https://example.com/changelog
```


[Add Firecrawl to ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a314a73f8ac819195b0d55e36b9c609?q=firecrawl)[Add Firecrawl to Claude](https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/firecrawl)


### How do you move your watches with the Firecrawl API?


The changedetection.io API lists your watches, and one Firecrawl SDK call turns their URLs into a monitor. Copy your changedetection.io API key from its settings page, then run this with both keys set:


```text
import   os


import   requests
from   firecrawl   import   Firecrawl


watches   =   requests  .  get  (
f  "  {  os.environ[  'CDIO_URL'  ]  }  /api/v1/watch"  ,
headers  =  {  "x-api-key"  : os.environ[  "CDIO_API_KEY"  ]},
timeout  =  30  ,
).  json  ()
urls   =   [watch  [  "url"  ]   for   watch   in   watches  .  values  ()   if   not   watch  [  "paused"  ]  ]


firecrawl   =   Firecrawl  (api_key  =  os.environ[  "FIRECRAWL_API_KEY"  ])
monitor   =   firecrawl  .  create_monitor  (
name  =  "Moved from changedetection.io"  ,
schedule  =  {  "text"  :   "every 6 hours"  },
goal  =  (
"Alert when a price, plan or new entry changes. "
"Ignore dates, banners and layout edits."
),
targets  =  [{  "type"  :   "scrape"  ,   "urls"  : urls}],
)


print  (  f  "Moved   {  len  (urls)  }   watches to monitor   {  monitor.id  }  "  )
print  (  "next run:"  , monitor.next_run_at)
print  (
"estimated Firecrawl credits per month:"  ,
monitor.estimated_credits_per_month,
)
```


The script moves your watch URLs. The monitor's schedule, goal and alert settings then take the place of changedetection.io's per-watch filters and notifications, so set them to match what you had. With two watches, the output looks like this:


```text
Moved 2 watches to monitor 01a2085e-42e7-718f-bf10-e1c52b400ac0
next run: 2026-11-23 18:00:00+00
estimated Firecrawl credits per month: 480
```


The estimate is an upper bound because it counts 1 Firecrawl credit per page per check plus 1 for judging, and the judge only charges for pages that changed.


The[Firecrawl CLI](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/sdks/cli) does the same for a single page, with` FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` set in your shell. Add` --email` to get email summaries:


```text
npx   firecrawl-cli@latest   monitor   create   --name   "Pricing page"   \
--page   https://www.firecrawl.dev/pricing   \
--schedule   "every 6 hours"   \
--goal   "Alert when any plan price or credit allowance changes"
```


For a restock or price watch, add a[change tracking](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/change-tracking) format in JSON mode to the target, with a schema for the fields you care about. The Node SDK, the REST API and the MCP server accept the same monitor settings, and the[step-by-step Firecrawl monitor guide](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/monitor-website-changes-firecrawl) walks through webhooks and a full test run.


### How much does Firecrawl /monitor cost?


Firecrawl /monitor has no per-monitor fee. Each check pays for the scrape, crawl or search it runs, plus an optional Firecrawl credit for each changed page the AI judge reviews.


What runs Cost per check


Page monitor (Markdown) 1 Firecrawl credit per URL


JSON mode for price and stock fields 4 more Firecrawl credits per page, 5 in total


Website monitor 1 Firecrawl credit per discovered page


Web-scale monitor 2 Firecrawl credits per 10 results, plus 1 per judged result


AI judging on page and website monitors 1 Firecrawl credit per changed page it reviews


Thirty pages checked once a day come to about 900 Firecrawl credits a month before judging, inside the free plan's 1,000. The[Hobby plan](https://www.firecrawl.dev/pricing) is $19 a month billed monthly for 5,000 Firecrawl credits, and every monitor returns its monthly credit estimate when you create it.


## Can you self-host a changedetection.io alternative?


Firecrawl, urlwatch and Huginn are the three changedetection.io alternatives on this list you can self-host. Firecrawl is open source under the AGPL-3.0 license, and Firecrawl Local is the lightest way to run it on your own machine.


**Firecrawl Local** is a single binary that scrapes, crawls and maps websites from your own computer, with no database, queue or container to run. It serves the Firecrawl API on localhost, so code written for Firecrawl runs against it unchanged, and it plugs into AI agents as an MCP server. For a full server, Firecrawl also ships a Docker Compose setup for its scrape, crawl, map and search APIs.

If you would rather not run a server at all, Firecrawl Cloud handles the schedule, JavaScript rendering, AI judging, email summaries and Slack alerts for you, with no model key to manage.


## Why do AI agents need more than a change alert?


AI agents act on what they read, so a useful alert carries the changed lines and a judgment on whether they matter. Firecrawl /monitor hands an agent the changed lines in text and JSON with an AI verdict, through webhooks or MCP tools, so the agent wakes only when a source it depends on changes.


More teams are running agents in production. In[McKinsey's state of AI survey from August 2026](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/the-state-of-ai) , **40%** of respondents at large organizations said they were scaling AI agents, up from 27% a year earlier. Buyers also care about connections. In[G2's 2026 AI agents report](https://sell.g2.com/g2-2026-ai-agents-insight-report) , a survey of 1,019 B2B decision-makers, **72%** called a strong ecosystem of connectors, actions or skills very important or a must-have for adopting agents.


[Minimal](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/how-minimal-builds-ai-support-agents-with-firecrawl) shows the pattern. Its AI support agents answer from each merchant's live storefront, and Firecrawl re-scrapes nearly six million storefront pages a month so those answers stay current.


> Storefronts come to us in every shape imaginable, and no matter the complexity, Firecrawl turns each one into clean, structured data our AI support agents can answer from.


—[Niek Hogenboom](https://www.linkedin.com/in/niek-hogenboom/) , Co-Founder at[Minimal](https://gominimal.ai/)


## Which changedetection.io alternative should you pick?


The right changedetection.io alternative depends on who reads the alert and who runs the software. Firecrawl /monitor covers email alerts, AI-judged changes and agent workflows without a server, changedetection.io and Firecrawl both run on your own hardware, and Visualping, Distill.io, urlwatch and Huginn each fit a narrower job.


Job Pick Why


Email me when a page changes Firecrawl /monitor Email summaries, AI judging included, setup from the dashboard or ChatGPT, Claude and Grok Bot


Give an AI agent or pipeline the diff Firecrawl /monitor Webhooks and MCP tools with text and JSON diffs plus an AI verdict


Track prices and restocks Firecrawl /monitor JSON mode Previous and current value for each field you define


Watch a whole site Firecrawl website monitor Added, changed and removed pages on every check


Run it on my own server changedetection.io or the Firecrawl engine Both are open source and run with Docker; Firecrawl self-hosts its scrape, crawl, map and search APIs


See visual changes on a few pages Visualping Hosted visual and text comparisons


Check pages from my own browser Distill.io Local monitors in the extension


Keep every watch in a config file urlwatch Config-file jobs run from cron


Turn a change into a chain of actions Huginn Agents that pass events to the next step


Competitor pricing pages are a common first watch. The[competitor monitoring guide](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/competitor-monitoring-firecrawl) sets one up end to end, the[Black Friday price tracker](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/black-friday-price-tracker) applies it to retail prices, and the[change detection deep dive](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/web-scraping-change-detection-with-firecrawl) shows how Firecrawl compares two versions of a page.


You can try Firecrawl /scrape with no API key through[keyless access](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/firecrawl-keyless-launch) . Monitors need a free account, which includes 1,000 Firecrawl credits a month on the[free plan](https://www.firecrawl.dev/pricing) , and you can create your first one from the[Firecrawl /monitor](https://www.firecrawl.dev/monitor) page.
